# Judges Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_282.jpg, JDG_page_283.jpg

1. And the sons of Yisrael again did the evil in the eyes of YHWH, and YHWH gave them into the hand of the P'lishtim forty years.

2. And there was a certain man from Tsor'ah, from the clan of the Danite, and his name [was] Manoach. And his wife [was] barren and had not borne [children].

3. And the messenger of YHWH appeared to the woman and said to her, "Behold now, you [are] barren and have not borne [children]. But you shall conceive and bear a son.

4. And now, be careful, I pray, and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.

5. For behold, you [are] conceiving and bearing a son. And a razor shall not go up upon his head, for a Nazirite of God the youth shall be from the womb. And he shall begin to save Yisrael from the hand of the P'lishtim."

6. And the woman came and said to her husband, saying, "A man of God came to me, and his appearance [was] like the appearance of the messenger of God, very awesome. And I did not ask him from where he [was], and his name he did not tell me.

7. And he said to me, 'Behold, you [are] conceiving and bearing a son. And now, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, for a Nazirite of God the youth shall be from the womb until the day of his death.'"

8. And Manoach entreated YHWH and said, "Please, my Lord, the man of God whom you sent — let him come again to us and teach us what we shall do for the youth who will be born."

9. And God listened to the voice of Manoach, and the messenger of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field. And Manoach her husband was not with her.

10. And the woman hurried and ran and told her husband and said to him, "Behold, the man has appeared to me — the one who came to me [the other] day."

11. And Manoach arose and went after his wife and came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And he said, "I [am]."

12. And Manoach said, "Now, when your words come [true], what shall be the rule for the youth, and what shall be done with him?"

13. And the messenger of YHWH said to Manoach, "From all that I said to the woman, let her be careful.

14. From anything that comes from the vine of wine she shall not eat, and wine and strong drink she shall not drink, and anything unclean she shall not eat. All that I commanded her, let her observe."

15. And Manoach said to the messenger of YHWH, "Let us detain you, I pray, and prepare before you a kid of the goats."

16. And the messenger of YHWH said to Manoach, "If you detain me, I will not eat your food. And if you prepare a burnt offering — to YHWH you shall offer it." For Manoach did not know that he [was] the messenger of YHWH.

17. And Manoach said to the messenger of YHWH, "What [is] your name, so that when your words come [true], we may honor you?"

18. And the messenger of YHWH said to him, "Why do you ask my name? And it [is] wonderful."

19. And Manoach took the kid of the goats and the grain offering and offered [it] up on the rock to YHWH. And [he was] doing a wonderful thing, and Manoach and his wife were watching.

20. And it was, when the flame went up from upon the altar toward the heavens, the messenger of YHWH went up in the flame of the altar. And Manoach and his wife were watching, and they fell on their faces to the ground.

21. And the messenger of YHWH did not again appear to Manoach and to his wife. Then Manoach knew that he [was] the messenger of YHWH.

22. And Manoach said to his wife, "We shall surely die, for we have seen God."

23. And his wife said to him, "If YHWH had desired to kill us, he would not have taken from our hand a burnt offering and a grain offering, and he would not have shown us all these [things], and at this time he would not have let us hear such [things] as these."

24. And the woman bore a son and called his name Shimshon. And the youth grew, and YHWH blessed him.

25. And the Spirit of YHWH began to stir him in Machaneh-Dan, between Tsor'ah and Eshta'ol.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.5 — "he shall begin to save":** v'hu yachel l'hoshia — only "begin." Samson will not complete the deliverance from the Philistines. That awaits David's wars. The verb is deliberately partial.

2. **v.18 — "And it is wonderful":** v'hu peli — from the root pala', "to be wonderful/incomprehensible." The angel's name is not a name but a description: it is beyond human comprehension. Cf. Isaiah 9:5, where the Messiah is called pele yo'ets ("Wonderful Counselor").

3. **v.25 — "began to stir him":** vatachel ruach YHWH l'fa'amo — the verb pa'am means "to thrust/beat/stir." The Spirit begins to agitate Samson like a bell being struck. This is different from the Spirit "being upon" (Othniel, Jephthah), "clothing" (Gideon), or "rushing upon" (which will come in ch.14).

— EMET, AI Translator
